prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1116; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim reference.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving on the main road in Baytown, heading toward the freeway. Traffic had slowed down a little ahead of me.

Q: Were you stopped or moving when you were hit?

A: I was stopped at a light. I had been sitting there for maybe ten seconds when I felt a hard jolt from behind.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before impact?

A: No. I was looking forward at the light. I only saw it in my mirror after it hit me, and by then it was too late.

Q: Did you exchange information with the other driver?

A: Yes, we swapped insurance and contact details at the scene. The driver seemed apologetic and said they had looked down at their phone.

Q: Did you feel any injury right after the collision?

A: My neck was stiff, but I didn't think much of it. By the next morning my right shoulder was really sore, and I couldn't lift my arm above my head.

Q: Have you seen a doctor for the shoulder?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care the following day. They took X-rays and told me to follow up with an orthopedic specialist for further evaluation.

Q: Are you still experiencing pain or limited movement?

A: Yes. Lifting groceries and sleeping on that side are difficult. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week.

Q: Is there anything else you would like to add?

A: Only that I was following the rules and I just want my car repaired and my medical bills taken care of.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.

A: Thank you.
